title: HB1562 (2018 Regular): Peace Orders and Protective Orders – Surrender of Firearms

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2018RS/bills/hb/hb1562f.pdf)
provenance.note: As filed. Bracketed words deleted from existing law: the discretionary firearm clause in Family Law § 4-505(a)(2)(viii) (replaced by mandatory new § 4-505(F)) and part of § 4-506(f)(1). The bill text as printed carries drafting slips (e.g. § 4-506(f) refers to 'TEMPORARY PEACE ORDER'; § 4-505 appears under the 4-506 heading); quotes follow the printed text. Family Law § 4-509 penalty cross-reference is also changed. No vote listed.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Courts and Judicial Proceedings § 3-1504(a)(4)(I)): THE TEMPORARY PEACE ORDER SHALL ORDER THE RESPONDENT TO: 1. SURRENDER TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ANY FIREARM IN THE RESPONDENT’S POSSESSION WITHIN 24 HOURS AFTER SERVICE OF THE PROTECTIVE ORDER; AND 2. REFRAIN FROM POSSESSION OF ANY FIREARM FOR THE DURATION OF THE TEMPORARY PEACE ORDER.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Courts and Judicial Proceedings § 3-1504(a)(4)(III)): 1. IF THE RESPONDENT FAILS TO SURRENDER A FIREARM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THIS PARAGRAPH, A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SHALL ACCOMPANY THE RESPONDENT TO THE PLACE WHERE THE FIREARM IS LOCATED AND TAKE CUSTODY OF THE FIREARM. 2. IF THE RESPONDENT FAILS TO SURRENDER A FIREARM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THIS PARAGRAPH AND THE RESPONDENT IS PROHIBITED FROM ENTERING THE LOCATION WHERE THE FIREARM IS LOCATED, THE LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SHALL SEIZE THE FIREARM.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Courts and Judicial Proceedings § 3-1505(d)(3)(I)): THE PEACE ORDER SHALL ORDER THE RESPONDENT TO: 1. SURRENDER TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ANY FIREARM IN THE RESPONDENT’S POSSESSION WITHIN 24 HOURS AFTER SERVICE OF THE PROTECTIVE ORDER; AND 2. REFRAIN FROM POSSESSION OF ANY FIREARM FOR THE DURATION OF THE PEACE ORDER.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Family Law § 4-505(F)(1)): THE TEMPORARY PROTECTIVE ORDER SHALL ORDER THE RESPONDENT TO: (I) SURRENDER TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ANY FIREARM IN THE RESPONDENT’S POSSESSION WITHIN 24 HOURS AFTER SERVICE OF THE PROTECTIVE ORDER; AND (II) REFRAIN FROM POSSESSION OF ANY FIREARM FOR THE DURATION OF THE TEMPORARY PROTECTIVE ORDER.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Family Law § 4-505(F)(3)(I)): IF THE RESPONDENT FAILS TO SURRENDER A FIREARM IN ACCORDANCE WITH THIS SUBSECTION, A LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER SHALL ACCOMPANY THE RESPONDENT TO THE PLACE WHERE THE FIREARM IS LOCATED AND TAKE CUSTODY OF THE FIREARM.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Family Law § 4-506(f)(1)(I)): SURRENDER TO LAW ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITIES ANY FIREARM IN THE RESPONDENT’S POSSESSION WITHIN 24 HOURS AFTER SERVICE OF THE PROTECTIVE ORDER;
